entry.idea: Clean power that runs around the clock is hard to get from wind or solar alone, so Mazama Energy drills three miles underground to reach superhot rock and turn it into steady geothermal electricity.
entry.lesson: When existing clean energy sources cannot run around the clock, adapting a proven technique, here oil-and-gas-style drilling, to reach a hotter, deeper resource can create a new always-on power source.
entry.name: Mazama Energy

growth.basis: substitute: $135M funding round led by Khosla Ventures
growth.reason: A large $135M round from a leading climate investor is a strong signal, though there is no revenue or customer number yet.

market.reason: Round-the-clock clean power is a large, worldwide need for grids and industry, not just a local niche.

tech.reason: Drilling three miles down to reach some of the hottest engineered geothermal rock attempted is a hard engineering feat few teams could match quickly.

entry.twist: It says a single well can generate 15 MW of power 24 hours a day, by drilling deeper and into hotter rock than typical geothermal projects reach.
entry.who_pays: Utilities and large power buyers, such as data center operators, that need steady, round-the-clock clean electricity.
entry.why_now: Data centers and power grids need more always-on clean electricity, and drilling technology has advanced enough to reach the extreme heat needed to make superhot-rock geothermal work.
